title: I built myself an AI-to-asset renderer with Opus behind the wheel, and this cozy otter game became the perfect case study
author: toreanjoel
selftext:
It's a rainy night in my cozy game concept, so my otter is staying in with raw fish and berries for dinner 🐟

https://reddit.com/link/1wpsmlh/video/oiuz2bvn6nrh1/player

The real story is how the scene was made: I've been building an AI-to-asset renderer that takes and image or just a prompt and turns them into 2D game ready assets all baked with Normals, height maps, an atlas, animations etc. Using it inside of the ThreeJS library and it starts to look the part for the category.

**Play the demo:** [https://www.crazygames.com/game/island-keeper](https://www.crazygames.com/game/island-keeper)  
**More about the game and where it's heading:** [https://keeper.nullhaven.studio/](https://keeper.nullhaven.studio/)

Next up, I'm ironing out a few performance issues.

Is anyone else building tooling to improve their asset output? I'd love to see what others are using in their workflows.
